stories.title: India unemployment rate falls to 5.1% in July‑September
stories.summary: The Economic Times says India's overall unemployment rate dropped to 5.1% in the July‑September quarter, marking a decline from the previous period. The article attributes the fall primarily to a decrease in rural joblessness, but offers no additional statistics or analysis and suggests the trend may reflect seasonal hiring patterns.
stories.why: Lower unemployment can boost consumer confidence and guide policy decisions.

stories.title: OpenAI, Anthropic face new oversight as New York’s AI safety law takes effect
stories.summary: The state opened a registration portal Tuesday, with which large frontier AI developers like Anthropic and OpenAI will be required to register by January 1, 2027. It mandates that large frontier developers — companies with more than $500 million in annual revenue — have to publish safety frameworks on their websites, report critical safety incidents within 72 hours, and issue public model transparency reports.
stories.why: This matters because it could change AI capabilities, costs, adoption, regulation or competitive positioning.
stories.previousTitle: New York launches registration portal for large AI developers under RAISE Act
stories.previousSummary: New York opened a registration portal on Tuesday, requiring “large frontier” AI developers—companies with over $500 million in annual revenue such as Anthropic and OpenAI—to register by Jan 1 2027. The RAISE Act, effective at the start of the year, requires them to publish safety frameworks, report critical safety incidents within 72 hours, and issue model‑transparency reports. The new Office of Digital Innovation, Governance, Integrity, and Trust (DIGIT) will enforce the law, with penalties up to $1 million for a first violation and $3 million for later ones.

stories.title: Google broadens its AI hardware portfolio with two new specialized chips
stories.summary: Google is notching up its chipmaking game as the company seeks to reduce its dependence on chips made by other companies for its cloud computing business. Google on Monday unveiled two new variants of its tensor processing units (TPUs), in-house-developed chips meant for AI workloads, that broaden its chip portfolio to additional use cases: confidential inference and more memory capacity for large workloads.
